meta.title: News Reader – Self-hosted RSS Reader with Encrypted Sync
meta.description: Open-source RSS reader for phone and desktop: read now, later or skip. End-to-end encrypted sync, no account. A Feedly alternative you can host yourself.

hero.read_what_matters_skip: Read what matters. Skip the rest.
hero.news_is_a_calm: News is a calm RSS reader for your phone and your desktop. No endless timeline, no algorithm – every new entry gets one decision: read now, later or not interested. Your devices stay in sync, end-to-end encrypted, without an account.
hero.free_amp_open_source: Free & open source · installable web app · works offline
hero.the_quiet_comeback_of: The quiet comeback of RSS in 2026
hero.new_cycle_lanes_along: New cycle lanes along the river from October
hero.measuring_the_energy_cost: Measuring the energy cost of a single web request
hero.device_label: The News app: an inbox with three entries, each with the actions read now, later and not interested, and a sync status reading ‘Synced’

reader.most_readers_pile_up: Most readers pile up unread counts until you give up. News works like a good editor: everything new lands in the inbox, and every entry leaves it again – with a decision.
reader.new_entries_from_all: New entries from all your sources, newest first. Nothing is marked read behind your back.
reader.opens_the_article_when: Opens the article. When you are through, it goes to Done. o
reader.your_reading_list_on: Your reading list – on every device, even after the entry left its feed. <kbd>l</kbd>
reader.gone_without_guilt_one: Gone, without guilt. One swipe on the phone, one key on the desktop. <kbd>x</kbd>

features.everything_a_reader_needs: Everything an RSS reader needs. Nothing it doesn't.
features.no_ads_no_tracking: No ads, no tracking, no feeds you didn't ask for – just your sources, in one calm place.
features.install_news_from_the: Install News from the browser like an app. Swipe to triage on the phone, use j k o l x on the desktop, share any page to News to follow it.
features.pair_a_device_by: Pair a device by scanning a QR code. Feeds, reading list and states are encrypted before they leave your device.
features.everything_lives_in_your: Everything lives in your browser. News starts instantly, works on the train and syncs when you are back online.
features.follow_any_website_the: Follow any website – the built-in Collector finds its entries even when the site never offered RSS.
features.import_your_opml_export: Import your OPML export and every source moves over. Export works just as easily – you can leave any time.
features.no_analytics_no_third: No analytics, no third-party requests, self-hosted fonts, no framework. A few kilobytes of plain JavaScript.

sync.sync_that_has_nothing: Sync that has nothing to leak.
sync.your_devices_share_one: Your devices share one secret key – passed on by QR code, never sent to the server. Everything is encrypted before it leaves your device. The server keeps a single sealed file per vault. No database, no account, no e-mail.
sync.aes_256_gcm_keys: – AES-256-GCM, keys derived on your devices only.
sync.one_opaque_file_per: – one opaque file per vault, nothing to query, dump or breach.
sync.one_endpoint_three_verbs: – one endpoint, three verbs, size and rate limits, no business logic.
sync.delete_with_one_click: – delete with one click; untouched vaults expire after 180 days.
sync.phone_and_laptop_hold: Phone and laptop hold the key and exchange only an encrypted blob through the server, which cannot read it

collector.most_readers_give_up: Most readers give up when a site has no RSS link. News doesn't – thanks to the Collector, a small REST endpoint on the same server. It tries the most precise strategy first, falls back step by step and always returns the same clean JSON. Use it for News, or build your own reader on top.
collector.the_url_already_is: The URL already is a feed. Parsed as-is – the fastest and most precise path.
collector.the_page_declares_its: The page declares its feed – via <link rel="alternate"> or a visible …/rss.xml link. The Collector follows it.
collector.nothing_declared_the_collector: Nothing declared? The Collector probes the usual suspects: /feed, /rss.xml, /feed.xml, /atom.xml, /index.xml …
collector.sitemap_desc: No feed? The sitemap, found via robots.txt and filtered to the requested path – used when its entries carry dates. Titles are taken from the page where possible.
collector.html_desc: The last resort: entries are extracted from the page itself – JSON-LD, <article> elements or links below the requested path.
collector.direct_url_is_a: direct URL is a native feed
collector.discovered_feed_declared_in: discovered Feed declared in the HTML
collector.guessed_feed_found_at: guessed Feed found at a common path
collector.sitemap_entries_built_from: sitemap Entries built from the sitemap
collector.html_article_entries_extracted: html-article Entries extracted from the page
collector.fact_ssrf: SSRF-safe – private hosts blocked, every redirect re-checked

build.your_server_your_name: Your server. Your name. Your readers.
build.news_reader_is_open: News Reader is a self-hosted RSS reader, open source under the MIT license. Host it for yourself, your family, your team or your community – under your own domain and your own brand. White-label is not an add-on: it is one theme file.
build.a_handful_of_php: A handful of PHP files and a static web app. No database server, no build step, no container required.
build.colours_and_fonts_live: Colours and fonts live in app/theme.css. Swap the icons and the app name in the manifest – done. Your users see your reader, not ours.
build.any_web_server_with: Any web server with PHP 8.1+ and HTTPS. The included nginx config blocks everything but the app and the API.
build.requires_php_8_1: Requires PHP 8.1+ with dom, libxml, mbstring (curl recommended) and a writable var/. That's all.

faq.news_is_a_calm: News is a calm feed reader for your phone and your desktop browser. Every new entry lands in the inbox and gets one decision: read now, later or not interested. It is an installable web app, works offline and is free and open source.
faq.how_is_it_different: How is it different from Feedly and co.?
faq.no_account_no_ads: No account, no ads, no tracking and no algorithm deciding what you see. Your reading state lives on your devices, sync is end-to-end encrypted, and you can run the whole thing on your own server.
faq.how_does_sync_work: How does sync work without an account?
faq.the_first_device_creates: The first device creates a random vault key. Other devices join by scanning a QR code or opening the pairing link. From that key each device derives an access token and an encryption key. The server only ever receives the token and one encrypted file – the key itself never leaves your devices.
faq.can_the_server_operator: Can the server operator read my feeds or reading list?
faq.no_feeds_reading_list: No. Feeds, reading list and states are encrypted with AES-256-GCM on your device before upload. The server stores one sealed file per vault, named after a hash of the access token. There is no database and nothing readable to leak. Like every website, the web server still sees your IP address when you connect.
faq.what_if_i_lose: What if I lose all my devices?
faq.then_the_vault_cannot: Then the vault cannot be decrypted – not even by us. That is the price of real end-to-end encryption. Export your subscriptions as OPML from time to time if you want a backup.
faq.the_collector_is_the: The Collector is the REST endpoint that ships with News Reader: GET /api/collect?url=… turns any website or feed URL into normalized JSON entries. It tries a native feed first, then a declared feed, common feed paths, the sitemap and finally the page's HTML.
faq.what_if_a_website: What if a website has no RSS feed?
faq.news_can_still_follow: News can still follow it. The Collector uses the site's sitemap if it carries dates, and otherwise extracts entries from the page itself (JSON-LD, article elements or links below the requested path).
faq.can_i_host_my: Can I host my own News Reader under my own brand?
faq.yes_it_is_mit: Yes. It is MIT-licensed. Colours and fonts live in one theme file, the name and icons in the web app manifest. Run it for yourself, your family, your team or your readers, under your own domain.
faq.what_do_i_need: What do I need to host it?
faq.php_8_1_with: PHP 8.1+ with dom, libxml and mbstring (curl recommended), a web server with HTTPS and a writable var/ folder. No database server, no build step, no background workers. An nginx config is included.
faq.yes_export_your_subscriptions: Yes. Export your subscriptions from Feedly as OPML and import the file in News under Feeds. News exports OPML as well, so you can leave any time.

final.open_news_in_your: Open News in your browser, follow your first site and install it on your phone. Or run your own News Reader – for you, your team or your readers.
